questions.question: Your React page is slow — how do you diagnose and fix frontend performance issues?
questions.title: Performance Frontend Scenarios
questions.direct_answer: Diagnose before optimizing: React DevTools Profiler for render causes, browser Performance tab for scripting/layout/paint, Network tab for payload. The usual culprits and fixes: too many re-renders (memo, stable props, state colocation, split contexts), expensive computation per render (useMemo), large lists (windowing/virtualization), unoptimized assets (code-splitting, lazy loading, image formats), and layout thrashing (batch DOM reads/writes). Optimize the measured bottleneck, verify with the same tool, stop.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you can debug performance frontend scenarios systematically rather than guessing.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Jumping to fixes without reproducing or measuring first.

The usual culprits and fixes: too many re-renders (memo, stable props, state colocation, split contexts), expensive computation per render (useMemo), large lists (windowing/virtualization), unoptimized assets (code-splitting, lazy loading, image formats), and layout thrashing (batch DOM reads/writes). Optimize the measured bottleneck, verify with the same tool, stop.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The process, in measurement order:

```
1. MEASURE — never optimize on theory
   • React Profiler: record the slow interaction → flame chart shows
     WHICH component, how long, and WHY ('props changed', 'hook 1 changed')
   • Performance tab: is time in Scripting (JS), Rendering (layout), or Painting?
   • Network: is the initial load the actual problem, not runtime?

2. CATEGORIZE the finding:
   Rendering problem          → React render volume
   Scripting problem           → computation, JSON parsing, big data
   Loading problem             → bundle size, waterfall requests
   Layout/paint problem        → CSS, DOM size, thrashing
```

The React render fixes (the most common category), by cost ascending:
```jsx
// 1. State colocation — move state DOWN to where it changes
//    a search input re-rendering the whole page = misplaced state
const SearchInput = () => { const [q, setQ] = useState(''); ... }  // local

// 2. Stable props — inline object/function props defeat memo
<Expensive onClick={() => ...} style={{...}} />   // new refs every render
// fix: useCallback, useMemo, or module-level constants

// 3. React.memo where profiling PROVED a re-render storm
const Row = React.memo(({ item }) => ...);

// 4. Split context — one changing value re-renders all consumers
//    split the frequently-changing slice into its own context
```

The non-React fixes (name them — they're often the real bottleneck): virtualized lists (react-window — render 20 visible rows of 10,000), code-splitting (React.lazy + Suspense per route), debouncing user-triggered work (search-as-you-type), moving heavy compute to a Worker, and image/bundle payload (the Network tab's finding — lazy-load below-the-fold, serve AVIF/WebP).

The discipline that separates seniors (the close): one change at a time, re-measure with the same tool after each, and keep the fix only if the number moved. Memoize-on-suspicion without measurement is how codebases fill with useMemo noise that helps nothing.

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S[slow page] --> M{measure: Profiler / Perf tab / Network}
    M -->|render storm| R[colocate state, stable props, memo, split context]
    M -->|scripting| C[useMemo, debounce, Worker, smaller data]
    M -->|loading| L[code-split, lazy, image formats, cache]
    M -->|layout/paint| P[contain, transform animation, smaller DOM]
    R & C & L & P --> V[re-measure → keep only if number moved]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
Why re-render volume is React's characteristic cost (the model): every state change re-runs the component function and (by default) its whole subtree — the render phase builds new element trees (cheap-ish) but reconciliation and effects scale with component count. The three multipliers: state placed too high (every keystroke re-renders the page), unstable props (inline functions/objects give memo nothing to skip), and context holding frequently-changing values (all consumers re-render). This is why 'my app got slow as it grew' is almost always render-volume, not slow individual components.

The interaction-to-paint pipeline (the browser reality React sits inside): input handler → React render+commit (scripting) → browser layout (reflow) → paint → composite. Long tasks block the main thread past the 50ms responsiveness budget; the Profiler's flame chart vs the Performance tab's layers tell you which stage eats the time. The fix differs by stage: scripting → less JS per render or move it off-thread; layout → smaller DOM, avoid thrashing (interleaved read/write of layout properties); paint/composite → CSS containment, transform-based animation, will-change on the animated layer.

The Core Web Vitals frame (the metrics that make this business-relevant): LCP (loading — image/asset optimization, preload the hero image), INP (interaction latency — the long-task/50ms story above), CLS (layout shift — size images/ads/embeds before load). Framing perf work in these terms connects 'slow page' to user-visible numbers and gives the before/after proof the discipline requires.
